text: Hedera Agent Ops. An on-chain registry for autonomous agents, where every action leaves a receipt that nobody can quietly delete.

A registry can tell you an agent exists. It cannot tell you what that agent has actually done. And once a registry has more entries than anyone can check by hand, that second question is the one that matters.

Here is how it works. A registered agent calls the Action Router. The router checks the agent's spend policy, then hands the work to an adapter. One adapter swaps on SaucerSwap. The other supplies and withdraws on Bonzo. Adding a protocol means adding an adapter, never editing the router.

Three roles are deliberately separate. The controller sets policy. The operator submits actions. The treasury holds the funds. An agent's hot key will eventually leak. When it does, the attacker can spend up to a limit a human already approved, and not one token more. That limit is enforced in the contract, not in the user interface.

The frontend writes, not just reads. Register an agent, set per-token spend caps, approve the router, and execute a swap, all from the browser. Registration alone grants no spending ability. Authority is granted one asset at a time.

When the agent acts, the router authorises before any token moves, pulls funds for that single call, and measures what actually came back. It ignores what the adapter claims. Then it emits an Action Executed receipt, unconditionally, in the same transaction as the transfer. It cannot be omitted without reverting the action itself.

That is why receipts are contract events, not messages an operator has to choose to submit. The app replays them from the Hedera mirror node, a week at a time, and anyone can point it at their own mirror node to check the trail independently.
This is deployed on Hedera testnet. The registry, the router, and both adapters are wired and source verified, with the wiring read back off chain rather than trusted from the deploy output.
Hedera Agent Ops. Agents that act on real DeFi, under limits the chain enforces, with a record the chain keeps. Thank you.
